# Jubilees Chapter 24 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Isaac at the Wells; Esau Sells the Birthright

---

**24:1** After the death of Abraham, the LORD blessed his son Isaac. Isaac arose from Hebron and went to dwell at the well of the vision in the first year of the third week of the forty-third jubilee.

**24:2** In the first year of the fourth week a famine arose in the land — a second famine, besides the first which had come in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Gerar, to the king of the Philistines.

**24:3** The LORD appeared to him and said: "Do not go down to Egypt. Dwell in the land I tell you, and sojourn in this land. I will be with you and bless you, for I will give all these lands to you and to your seed, and I will establish the oath I swore to Abraham your father. I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens and as the sand on the seashore.

**24:4** Your seed shall inherit all these lands, and all the nations of the earth shall bless themselves by your seed — because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge: my commandments, my statutes, and my laws."

**24:5** Isaac dwelt in Gerar for three weeks of years.

**24:6** Abimelech the king of the Philistines gave orders concerning Isaac, saying: "He is my brother" — for he feared to kill him on account of his wife Rebekah, since she was beautiful.

**24:7** Isaac prospered greatly among the Philistines and accumulated much property — flocks of sheep, herds of cattle, and donkeys. He sowed in the land of the Philistines and reaped a hundredfold, and Isaac grew exceedingly great, and the Philistines envied him.

**24:8** Now all the wells that Abraham's servants had dug in Abraham's lifetime, the Philistines had stopped them up after Abraham's death and filled them with earth.

**24:9** Abimelech said to Isaac: "Move away from us, for you have become far greater than we are." Isaac departed from there in the first year of the seventh week and sojourned in the valleys of Gerar.

**24:10** They dug again the wells of water that Abraham's servants had dug in Abraham's lifetime, which the Philistines had stopped up after his death, and called them by the names that Abraham his father had given them.

**24:11** Isaac's servants dug a well in the valley and found spring water there. The herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with the herdsmen of Isaac, saying: "The water belongs to us." So Isaac called the name of that well Esek — Contention — for they had contended with him there.

**24:12** They dug another well, and they quarreled over that one too. Isaac called it Sitnah — Enmity.

**24:13** He moved on from there and dug another well, and no one quarreled over it. Isaac called it Rehoboth — Spaciousness — and said: "For now the LORD has made room for us, and we will flourish in the land."

**24:14** He went up from there to the well of the oath in the second year of the seventh week.

**24:15** That night the LORD appeared to him and said: "I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not fear, for I am with you, and I will bless you and multiply your seed for the sake of Abraham my servant."

**24:16** Isaac built an altar there and called upon the name of the LORD. He pitched his tent there, and his servants dug a well.

**24:17** That same day the servants of Abimelech came to Isaac and said: "Let there be an oath between us — between us and you. Let us make a covenant with you: just as we have not harmed you, and have done you nothing but good and sent you away in peace — so now, you are blessed by the LORD."

**24:18** Isaac replied: "Why have you come to me? You hated me and drove me away from you." They said: "We have seen clearly that the LORD is with you. We said, 'Let there be an oath between us and you — a covenant — that you will not harm us, as we have not touched you or done you any harm but only good, and sent you away in peace. Now you are blessed by the LORD.'"

**24:19** Isaac prepared a feast for them and they ate and drank and departed. That day they swore an oath to one another. Then Isaac sent them away and they left in peace.

**24:20** That same day Esau came in from the field famished. Esau said to his brother Jacob: "Give me some of that red stew." Jacob said to his brother: "Sell me your birthright today."

**24:21** Esau said: "I am about to die — what use is a birthright to me?" Jacob said: "Swear to me today." Esau swore to him and sold his birthright to Jacob.

**24:22** Jacob gave his brother Esau bread and lentil stew. He ate and drank, rose up, and went his way. And Esau despised his birthright.

**24:23** In the seventh week, in its first year, Isaac sowed in the land of the Philistines and harvested a hundredfold. Isaac grew greater and greater until he was exceedingly great.

**24:24** In the second year of the seventh week a famine covered all the land except the land of the Philistines.

**24:25** The Philistines were jealous of Isaac's flocks and herds and all his possessions.

**24:26** Abimelech the king of the Philistines declared: "Know that everything you have is really ours. Now go from our land."

**24:27** Isaac departed from there into the valley and dug the wells anew.

**24:28** All these things happened in those days.

---
*LOGOS notes: Well names transliterated and translated: Esek (Contention, v.11), Sitnah (Enmity/Hostility, v.12), Rehoboth (Spaciousness/Room, v.13). The Jubilees account integrates the birthright sale into the Isaac-at-Gerar narrative. "Three weeks of years" = 21 years (v.5).*
